newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish rail engine drivers give up planned strike.
newsitem.headline: Polish rail engine drivers give up planned strike.

text.p: Poland's train drivers' trade union dropped plans for a pay strike after signing an agreement late on Thursday with the board of Polish State Railways (PKP), a railways spokeswoman said.

"Late on Thursday the Board of PKP signed an agreement with the rail engine drivers' trade union and the union decided to give up the strike which was to start on Saturday," Anna Raczkowska said in a statement.
The union wanted the PKP management to keep real wages at the current levels and to increase employment.

A new labour law, which came into effect on January 1, envisages working time and organisation changes which would decrease rail engine drivers' wages, Andrzej Krawczyk, head of PKP's social and employee department told Reuters.
"Therefore, we have agreed to compensate this group in other ways," he said.
Krawczyk added that the PKP board would meet with all unions operating in the company on January 31 and set the ceiling for wage growth in the firm in 1997.
